CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 3, audited at commit 0251e99 (committed; working tree carries only sprint bookkeeping moves). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. One required fix, in README.md. Everything else is met, and most of it is met well. REQUIRED FIX -- R5. The documented preview redirect entry matches hosts this project does not control. README.md's redirect table gives the preview entry as: https://my-little-racoon-*.vercel.app/** and argues it is safe because it is "scoped to hostnames starting with my-little-racoon-, not a bare *.vercel.app". The prefix is not the part that needs scoping. vercel.app is a shared namespace: an auto-generated deployment URL is --.vercel.app, and project names are per-account, not globally unique. Anyone can create a Vercel project named my-little-racoon-anything under their own team and get, for example, my-little-racoon-x-a1b2c3-attackerteam.vercel.app -- which matches the pattern above, because there are no dots between the prefix and .vercel.app for the glob to stop on. That is an entry matching a host outside this project's domains, which is exactly what R5's acceptance criterion prohibits, and the open-redirect risk the sprint file names with QA1 assigned to check it by name. I am the named check. It does not pass. The fix is to anchor the suffix on the Vercel team/scope slug, which an attacker cannot forge because it is their own account's slug, not yours: https://my-little-racoon-*-.vercel.app/** This is also the form Supabase's own documentation recommends for Vercel previews (https://*-username.vercel.app). It covers both auto-generated preview URLs and branch aliases (-git--.vercel.app), since both end in -.vercel.app. Keep the existing instruction to confirm the real pattern against this project's actual preview URLs -- just confirm the suffix as well as the prefix. Severity, honestly stated: there is no live exploit path in this diff today. Sign-in is signInWithPassword inside a server action redirecting internally to /account. There is no OAuth, no magic link, no email confirmation, no emailRedirectTo anywhere in the repository, so the redirect allowlist is currently unused. This is a required fix anyway, because it is the permanent, documented configuration guidance, Sprint 5 is where previews start being used for real, and a redirect allowlist is retrofitted badly and audited rarely. Fixing a table row now costs a minute. It is also, per the sprint file, the one security item this gate was specifically told to check. Requirements coverage: R1 MET as written, with a handoff gap -- see note 1. enable_signup = false in both [auth] and [auth.email] in supabase/config.toml, each with a comment saying why. No registration route, form, or signUp() call anywhere in the diff. R2 MET. Cookie-based throughout via @supabase/ssr createServerClient: lib/supabase/server.ts for server components/actions/route handlers, lib/supabase/proxy.ts for the refresh. No session state held client-side -- there is no "use client" component in the repository at all. Next 16 renamed middleware.ts to proxy.ts, and the build confirms it is actually wired up rather than sitting there inert: the route table prints "f Proxy (Middleware)". Both the refresh and the protected page call getUser(), not getSession(), and the reason is written down in the file -- getSession() only decodes the cookie, getUser() revalidates against the Auth server. That is the correct choice and the comment means the next person will not "simplify" it. R3 MET, verified by execution rather than by reading. app/account/page.tsx is a server component that awaits getUser() and redirects before returning any markup. Built the app and requested /account unauthenticated: HTTP 307, location: /sign-in, and grepping the response body for "Signed in as" and "Sign out" returns zero. The protected content is never produced, let alone shipped and hidden. R4 MET. All three environment classes are covered: local in config.toml, production and preview documented in README's table, with the Vercel preview hostname pattern present. The README is explicit that config.toml governs only the local stack and that the hosted allowlist is a separate dashboard setting -- which is true, easily missed, and the reason this section is worth having. R5 NOT MET. See the required fix above. R6 MET. New timestamped migration 20260816131120_add_user_id_to_readings.sql adds user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade, plus an index on it, plus the ledger insert this repo's convention requires. Grepped the whole tree at 0251e99 for DDL outside supabase/migrations/: zero hits. The comment stating that NOT NULL with no backfill is safe only because the table is empty, and not to repeat the move on a populated one, is the right thing to leave behind. Indexing user_id now rather than after Sprint 4's policies make every query slow is the kind of thing I do not usually get to write down as a positive. R7 MET. README covers the new variables question, creating the practitioner account, and per-environment redirect configuration. .env.example is unchanged, and that is correct rather than an omission: this sprint introduces no new environment variables, it reuses NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, both already listed and marked public. Grepped the diff for JWTs, sbp_ tokens, quoted passwords and credentialed connection strings: clean. Verified by execution: - lint, typecheck, test all exit 0. 8 tests across 3 files; the 3 new ones cover resolvePublicConfig's happy path and both missing-variable branches. - next build exits 0. Route table: / static; /account, /sign-in, /api/health/db dynamic; "f Proxy (Middleware)" present. - Rebuilt with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="QA1PROBESERVICEROLE" and grepped all of .next: absent from the entire build output. The new @supabase/ssr client correctly uses the anon key, not the service role key. - /account unauthenticated: 307 to /sign-in, no protected markup in the body. - The proxy does not fall over when Supabase is unreachable -- served the redirect cleanly against a nonexistent Supabase host rather than 500ing every route. Notes, not conditions: 1. HANDOFF ITEM, do not let this one fall through. Disabling sign-up on the hosted project is a dashboard action, and it is NOT in the sprint file's External dependencies, which list only the practitioner account and the redirect URLs. The README says it plainly ("the same setting must be turned off for the hosted project in the dashboard"), so this is a handoff gap rather than a code defect, and it is why R1 passes. But the failure is silent and it inverts the repository's own claim: config.toml would say sign-up is disabled everywhere while production quietly accepts public registration. Somebody needs to turn it off in the dashboard before this ships, and GroundTruth should verify it live -- an unauthenticated POST to /auth/v1/signup with the anon key should be refused. That is the same ten-second shape as the anon-rows check already carried into this sprint's GroundTruth criteria. Adding it is Master Controller's call, not mine. 2. lib/supabase/server.ts's comment still says "middleware.ts refreshes the session on every request". The file is proxy.ts now. One word, and comments that name files that do not exist are how the next person loses twenty minutes. 3. /sign-in renders searchParams.error straight into

. React escapes it, so this is not XSS -- I checked before raising it. It does let anyone craft a /sign-in?error=... link that shows the practitioner arbitrary text on a real sign-in page, which is a phishing primitive on a page where someone is about to type a password. Map to a fixed set of codes instead of reflecting the string. Cheap, and worth doing before any further auth UI is built on top of it. 4. Carried forward and still true: R2's local stack remains unverified here (no Docker on this machine), and the schema_migrations ledger still depends on every migration remembering its own insert, enforced by nothing. This sprint's migration remembered. Re-audit after the README fix. It is one table row and a sentence; keep the re-audit proportionate to that. Nothing in the code needs to move.
Scope creep - this is not an authenticated application
